faqs.q: What is the arch fender and what sizes does it come in?
faqs.a: The arch fender is a molded rubber fender for berths, jetties and tugs, in 6 sizes from 150 H × 1000 mm to 400 H × 3500 mm. It is sized by height and length.

faqs.q: How do I read the Indus part number on the arch fender?
faqs.a: In IH-LR-MF-AF-150HX1000MM, the suffix 150HX1000MM is the 150 H × 1000 mm size, and IH-LR-MF-AF-400HX3500MM ends in 400HX3500MM for 400 H × 3500 mm. Each size in the table has its own part number.

faqs.q: What dimensions does the arch fender table list?
faqs.a: Each size gives the height H and length L, for example 150 H × 1000 mm and 400 H × 3500 mm, with dimensions B, E, I and W in the table. Check the base width W and mounting dimensions against your berth structure.

faqs.q: How do I size a arch fender for a berth?
faqs.a: Size a fender on the berthing energy it must absorb and the reaction the hull and structure can take; send vessel and berth details for a selection. For the arch fender, pick the row whose dimensions fit your structure and check the weight against your lifting plan.

faqs.q: What energy absorption and reaction force does the arch fender have?
faqs.a: The facts we hold give no energy absorption or reaction force for the arch fender. Size a fender on the berthing energy it must absorb and the reaction the hull and structure can take, and send the vessel and berth details so we can propose a selection.

faqs.q: What is the arch fender made of?
faqs.a: The arch fender is rubber, made by molded pressing. The facts we hold give no rubber grade or hardness, so ask for the manufacturer's data if your specification needs it.

faqs.q: Which standard or certificate applies to the arch fender?
faqs.a: No standard or certificate is named for the arch fender in our data. State any standard or test certificate you need on the RFQ, and we confirm what the manufacturer can supply.

faqs.q: What do I mount the arch fender with, and what goes beside it?
faqs.a: Fit the arch fender with the chains, bolts and backing on your structure, and see the [Marine Fenders shelf](/c/marine-fenders) for other fenders. For mooring on the same berth, see the [Bollards and Mooring shelf](/c/bollards-mooring).

faqs.q: How does energy absorption differ from reaction force on a arch fender?
faqs.a: For the arch fender, energy absorption is how much of the vessel's berthing energy the fender takes up as it compresses, and reaction force is the load it passes back into the hull and the quay. A good selection absorbs the energy required while keeping the reaction within what the hull and structure can carry.

faqs.a: In IH-LR-MF-WF2-DR280X540, the suffix DR280X540 is the DR 280×540 size, and IH-LR-MF-WF2-DR300X600 ends in DR300X600 for DR 300×600. Each size in the table has its own part number.

faqs.q: What dimensions does the wing fender table list?
faqs.a: Sizes are DR 280×540, DR 300×540 and DR 300×600, with dimensions B, D, G, H, M, P, Q and W in the table and weights of 125, 130 and 144 kg.

faqs.q: How do I size a wing fender for a berth?
faqs.a: Size a fender on the berthing energy it must absorb and the reaction the hull and structure can take; send vessel and berth details for a selection. For the wing fender, pick the row whose dimensions fit your structure and check the weight against your lifting plan.

faqs.q: What energy absorption and reaction force does the wing fender have?
faqs.a: The facts we hold give no energy absorption or reaction force for the wing fender. Size a fender on the berthing energy it must absorb and the reaction the hull and structure can take, and send the vessel and berth details so we can propose a selection.

faqs.q: What is the wing fender made of?
faqs.a: The facts we hold name no rubber grade for the wing fender. Ask for the manufacturer's data if your specification needs a grade or hardness.

faqs.q: Which standard or certificate applies to the wing fender?
faqs.a: No standard or certificate is named for the wing fender in our data. State any standard or test certificate you need on the RFQ, and we confirm what the manufacturer can supply.

faqs.q: What do I mount the wing fender with, and what goes beside it?
faqs.a: Fit the wing fender with the chains, bolts and backing on your structure, and see the [Marine Fenders shelf](/c/marine-fenders) for other fenders. For mooring on the same berth, see the [Bollards and Mooring shelf](/c/bollards-mooring).

faqs.q: How does energy absorption differ from reaction force on a wing fender?
faqs.a: For the wing fender, energy absorption is how much of the vessel's berthing energy the fender takes up as it compresses, and reaction force is the load it passes back into the hull and the quay. A good selection absorbs the energy required while keeping the reaction within what the hull and structure can carry.

faqs.q: Where is the wing fender used?
faqs.a: Wing fenders are used on berths, jetties and tugs along edges. See the [types of marine fenders](/blog/types-of-marine-fenders). Tell us the berth, the vessel and the structure and we propose a wing fender size.

faqs.q: Wing fender compared with the W fender?
faqs.a: The wing fender is listed in 3 DR sizes with a wide base. The [W fender](/p/w-fender) is listed in 4 sizes by profile. Choose on the profile and mounting.

faqs.q: Do you stock the wing fender, and how do I order?
faqs.a: Yes. The wing fender is in stock at our warehouse in Dubai, UAE, with worldwide shipping at the best lead times. Request a quote by sending the sizes you need through [our contact page](/contact).
